learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.exploration: Selected all four outcomes. Both swerve showed unilateral gains of 2; both straight showed gains of 10. Each asymmetric outcome said neither wants to switch. Reversible outcome buttons allowed comparison.
observations.reveal: Correction named One of each and traced every unilateral comparison: 1 to 3, -10 to 0, and the asymmetric players refusing 3 to 1 or 0 to -10. Scope stated invented payoffs, one round, simultaneous choices.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 inline screenshots inspected. Readable four-cell matrix, highlighted selected cell and red gain arrows. Reveal and table fit the viewport.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner explicitly said learning history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, metadata or other reviewers judgments inspected.

prediction.reason: A concrete commitment is elicited, but stable is not defined until exploration.

interaction.reason: All four outcomes expose the causal unilateral-switch test.
interaction.evidence: Compared stable asymmetric cells with both symmetric cells.

payoff.reason: Explanation resolves the symmetry intuition with explicit comparisons.

clarity.reason: Arrows and numbers make stability legible with a clear toy scope.
clarity.evidence: Invented, simultaneous, one-round qualifier remains visible.

transfer.reason: A reusable unilateral-switch principle appears without a new application.
transfer.evidence: Only the original four outcomes are assessed.

accessibility.reason: No full accessibility mode audit performed.
accessibility.evidence: Visual screenshots and ordinary click interaction only.

surprise.reason: Identical players have different stable actions.

visualExplanation.reason: Gain arrows show why players leave a cell.

playfulness.reason: Exploring a familiar confrontation is moderately engaging.

practicalValue.reason: Offers a basic stability test in a constrained toy.

depth.reason: Separates symmetry of players from symmetry of outcomes.

complexity.reason: Reading a payoff matrix and holding the other player fixed requires a new reasoning habit.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Compare personal payoffs while changing only one action.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Four plainly labeled outcome buttons with no setup.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Two numbers per matrix cell and directional arrows.

whyCool: The same symmetric table yields two asymmetric stable outcomes.
caveat: Prediction uses stable before defining it; no fresh application tests generalization.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
